autoContext: Generates or revises a multi-stage Dockerfile (one stage per declared build step, one final stage per declared environment), grounded in evidence from any existing Dockerfiles in the repo (shared base image discovery) and any existing target Dockerfile (revision instead of blind overwrite), then runs a two-call security audit gated PASS/FAIL/FORCE before writing.

intake.prompt: Path to the Dockerfile, relative to the repo root (e.g. services/api/Dockerfile):
Build steps in order, comma-separated (e.g. install-deps, compile, run-tests, prune-devdeps). Each becomes its own build stage:
Target environments, comma-separated (e.g. dev, staging, production). Each gets its own final stage built FROM the last build stage:
Preferred base image and tag if you already know it (e.g. node:20-slim), or NONE to let discovery decide:

render.prompt:
Generate or revise a single multi-stage Dockerfile at path {dockerfile_path}.

SPECS:
  build steps, in order: {build_steps}
  target environments: {environments}
  base image hint: {base_image_hint}
  shared-base-image discovery result: {shared_image_findings}

If a Dockerfile already exists at this path, its current content is shown below — REVISE it in place, preserving any working, still-relevant instructions, rather than discarding it wholesale:
{current_dockerfile}

Rules:
1. Create ONE build stage per entry in build_steps, in the given order, each named after its step (e.g. "AS install-deps"), each stage building FROM the previous stage (first stage FROM the base image).
2. Base image selection: if shared_image_findings starts with "SHARED_BASE:", use that exact image:tag for the first stage unless base_image_hint explicitly overrides it. Otherwise use base_image_hint if it is not NONE. If both are unavailable, choose a minimal, actively-maintained official image appropriate to the project and say which one you picked in a comment at the top of the file.
3. Create ONE final stage per entry in environments, each named after its environment (e.g. "AS production"), each FROM the last build stage, containing only what that environment needs to run (no build toolchain, no test artifacts, no dev dependencies) — production-like environments must be the leanest.
4. Every stage that doesn't need root must run as a non-root USER. Never embed secrets, API keys, or credentials as ARG/ENV literals — reference build secrets via --mount=type=secret or runtime env injection instead, and say so in a comment.
5. Pin base image tags to a specific version, never :latest.

Emit the Dockerfile as one path-bearing fence at {dockerfile_path}.

After the Dockerfile fence, include ONE pathless bash fence that builds the FIRST stage listed in target environments ({environments}) as a smoke test, in exactly this form (substitute the real stage name and path):
docker build -f {dockerfile_path} --target <first-environment-name> -t dockerfile-builder-smoke-test .
No other commentary outside the fences.
